cards.q: On a scatter plot, the points go down from left to right and lie close to a straight line. What kind of correlation is this?
cards.why: Going down from left to right is negative; lying close to a straight line is strong. So it is a strong negative correlation.
cards.hook: Direction gives the sign; closeness to a line gives the strength.
keys: close to a straight line is strong

cards.q: Which of these could be a correlation coefficient?
cards.why: A correlation coefficient r is always between −1 and 1. Only −0.8 is in that range; 5, −1.5 and 1.2 are outside it.
cards.hook: r always lies between −1 and 1.

cards.q: For 20 teenagers, the correlation coefficient between height and arm span is 0.9. What does this tell you?
cards.right: Taller teens tend to have longer spans
wrong: Taller teens tend to have shorter spans
Height and arm span are hardly linked
cards.why: 0.9 is close to 1, so the link is strong, and it is positive: as height goes up, arm span goes up too.
cards.hook: Say the strength and the direction, in context.

cards.q: In a stem-and-leaf diagram the key is 1 | 9 = 19. What value does stem 4, leaf 3 stand for?
cards.why: The stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the units digit: stem 4, leaf 3 is 43.
cards.hook: Stem = tens, leaf = units. Always read the key.

cards.q: A stem-and-leaf plot of dogs' weights has the key 6 | 0 = 6.0 kg. What weight does stem 5, leaf 7 show?
cards.why: The key says the stem is whole kilograms and the leaf is tenths: stem 5, leaf 7 is 5.7 kg.
cards.hook: Read the key first: it tells you what the stem and the leaf are worth.

cards.q: 7 of the 28 employees in a business are in their 50s. What percentage of the employees is that?
cards.why: Write it as a fraction of all 28, then × 100: 7 ÷ 28 × 100 = 25%.
cards.hook: Percentage = part ÷ whole × 100.

cards.q: A country's energy use: oil 40%, gas 25%, coal 10%, other 5%, and the rest is renewable. What percentage is renewable?
cards.why: One country's percentages add up to 100%: 100 − 40 − 25 − 10 − 5 = 20%.
cards.hook: The parts of a whole add up to 100%.

cards.q: In a pie chart, what angle shows a group that is 15% of the total?
cards.why: The full circle, 360°, is 100%, so each 1% is 3.6°: 15 × 3.6 = 54°.
cards.hook: Pie chart: 100% is 360°, so 1% is 3.6°.

cards.q: Find the mean of 2, 5, 6, 9, 13.
cards.why: Add them: 2 + 5 + 6 + 9 + 13 = 35. Divide by how many there are (5): 35 ÷ 5 = 7.
cards.hook: Mean = total ÷ how many.

cards.q: Find the median of 8, 3, 11, 5, 9.
cards.why: Put them in order: 3, 5, 8, 9, 11. The median is the middle (3rd) value: 8.
cards.hook: Median: sort first, then take the middle.

cards.q: Find the range of 12, 5, 20, 9, 14.
cards.why: Range = largest − smallest = 20 − 5 = 15.
cards.hook: Range: biggest minus smallest, wherever they sit in the list.

cards.q: What does the standard deviation of a set of data measure?
cards.right: How spread out it is around the mean
cards.why: The standard deviation is a typical distance of the values from the mean: small means bunched together, big means spread out.
cards.hook: Standard deviation = spread around the mean.
keys: a typical distance of the values from the mean

cards.q: For normally distributed data, about what percentage lies within one standard deviation of the mean?
cards.why: The empirical rule: about 68% within 1 standard deviation, 95% within 2, 99.7% within 3.
cards.hook: 68, 95, 99.7: for 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations.

cards.q: Test scores are normal with mean 100 and standard deviation 20. About what percentage score between 60 and 140?
cards.why: 60 and 140 are each 40 = 2 × 20 from the mean: 2 standard deviations either side, so about 95%.
cards.hook: First ask: how many standard deviations from the mean?

cards.q: Sleep times are normal with mean 7.8 hours and standard deviation 0.6 hours. Between which values do the middle 68% lie?
cards.why: 68% is within 1 standard deviation of the mean: 7.8 − 0.6 = 7.2 h and 7.8 + 0.6 = 8.4 h.
cards.hook: Middle 68%: the mean ± 1 standard deviation.

cards.q: For a random sample of size n, what is the 95% margin of error for a population proportion?
cards.why: Margin of error = 1/√n. For example, n = 100 gives 1/√100 = 1/10 = 0.1 = 10%.
cards.hook: Margin of error: one over root n.

cards.q: A poll asks a random sample of 400 people. What is the 95% margin of error, as a percentage?
cards.hook: Square root first, then 1 over it, then × 100 for %.

cards.q: A poll gives 54% support, with a margin of error of 3.2%. What is the 95% confidence interval for the support?
cards.why: Go one margin of error below and above the sample result: 54 − 3.2 = 50.8 and 54 + 3.2 = 57.2.
cards.hook: Confidence interval = sample % ± margin of error.

cards.q: In a random sample of 300 people, 45 said yes. What percentage of the sample said yes?
cards.why: Sample proportion = 45 ÷ 300 = 0.15. Multiply by 100: 15%.
cards.hook: Proportion = the ones who said yes ÷ the sample size.

cards.q: A 95% confidence interval for the share of new cars that are electric is 9.5% ≤ p ≤ 16.5%. A reporter claims the share is 19.2%. What do you conclude?
wrong: Can't tell without the sample size
cards.why: 19.2% is outside 9.5% to 16.5%, so the sample doesn't support it: there is evidence the share is different. Reject the claim.
cards.hook: Claim inside the interval: no evidence. Outside: reject it.

cards.q: To estimate how long Irish students read each day, a group asked the first 200 students to arrive at one school on a Monday. What is the main problem?
cards.right: It isn't random, so it may be biased
wrong: A survey must ask every student
200 students is too many to ask
They should have asked on a Friday
cards.why: A good sample is random, so it represents all students in Ireland. Early arrivals at one school on one morning may not be typical.
cards.hook: Was everyone equally likely to be picked? If not, it may be biased.

cards.q: Data: minutes spent reading per day, grouped as 0–30, 30–60, 60–90 and so on. Which graph suits it best?
cards.why: Time is continuous and the classes are equal 30-minute intervals, so use a histogram: the bars touch, with no gaps.
cards.hook: Continuous data in classes → histogram, bars touching.
keys: the bars touch, with no gaps

cards.q: Scatter plots: A falls, close to a line; B rises, close to a line; C rises but is spread out. Their r values are 0.95, 0.6 and −0.95. Which matching is right?
cards.why: A goes down, so it is negative: −0.95. B and C go up. B hugs a line, so B is 0.95 (strong); C is more spread out, so 0.6.
cards.hook: Sign from the direction; size from how close the points are to a line.

cards.q: Stem-and-leaf (key 4 | 1 = 41): 4 | 1 2 3 3 9; 5 | 4 5 7 7 8; 6 | 3 4 5 5. How many of the values are more than 45?
cards.why: Above 45: on the 4 row only 49 (1 value), then all 5 of the 50s and all 4 of the 60s: 1 + 5 + 4 = 10.
cards.hook: Turn each leaf back into the full number before you count.

cards.q: Stem-and-leaf (key 1 | 5 = 15): 1 | 5 8 9; 2 | 0 3 6 7; 3 | 1 4. What is the median?
cards.why: 9 values, already in order. The median is the (9 + 1) ÷ 2 = 5th value: 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, so it is 23.
cards.hook: Median is value number (n + 1) ÷ 2. Stem-and-leaf is already sorted.

cards.q: Year A: 600 of 1000 tonnes of waste went to landfill. Year B: 450 of 900 tonnes did. What is the difference between the two landfill percentages?
cards.hook: Work out each percentage first, then subtract.

cards.q: A pie chart shows the grades of 72 students. 39 of them got Merit. What angle is the Merit sector?
cards.why: 360° shared by 72 students is 360 ÷ 72 = 5° each. Merit: 39 × 5 = 195°.
cards.hook: Angle = number ÷ total × 360°.

cards.q: A shelter has 40 animals: 14 cats and the rest dogs. 11 of the dogs are male. How many female dogs are there?
cards.why: Dogs: 40 − 14 = 26. Female dogs are the dogs that are not male: 26 − 11 = 15.
cards.hook: Two-way table: each row and column adds up to its total.

cards.q: Find the mean of 12, 7, 9, 15, 8, 10, 11, correct to 1 decimal place.
cards.why: Total: 72. Divide by 7: 72 ÷ 7 = 10.285… The next digit after the 2 is 8, so round up: 10.3.
cards.hook: Rounding: look at the next digit. 5 or more, round up.

cards.q: Find the median of 4, 9, 6, 12, 7, 14.
cards.why: In order: 4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 14. An even number of values, so go halfway between the middle two: (7 + 9) ÷ 2 = 8.
cards.hook: Even number of values? Median = halfway between the middle two.

cards.q: The list 8, 8, 9, 11, 14, 17, 28 has a median of 11. One more number is added and the new median is 10.5. What number was added?
cards.why: 8 numbers: the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th. 10.5 is between 9 and 11, so the middle two are x and 11: (x + 11) ÷ 2 = 10.5, x = 10.
cards.hook: Even count: the median is the average of the middle two.

cards.q: In a frequency table, the scores 1, 2 and 3 occur 5, 3 and 2 times. What is the mean score?
cards.hook: Frequency table: add up (value × frequency), then ÷ total frequency.

cards.q: The mean of four numbers is 50. Three of them are 40, 55 and 60. What is the fourth number?
cards.why: Four numbers with a mean of 50 add up to 4 × 50 = 200. The three you know add to 155, so the fourth is 200 − 155 = 45.
cards.hook: Mean × how many = the total.

cards.q: Heights are normally distributed, and 95% of them are between 150 cm and 170 cm. What are the mean and the standard deviation?
cards.why: The mean is halfway: (150 + 170) ÷ 2 = 160 cm. 95% spans 2 standard deviations each side, 4 in all: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm.
cards.hook: 95% spans 4 standard deviations: 2 below the mean and 2 above.

cards.q: Weights are normally distributed. The middle 68% are between 60 kg and 80 kg. What is the standard deviation?
cards.why: The middle 68% is 1 standard deviation either side of the mean, so 60 to 80 is 2 of them: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 kg.
cards.hook: Middle 68%: 2 standard deviations wide. Middle 95%: 4 wide.

cards.q: Sleep times are normal with mean 7.8 hours and standard deviation 0.6 hours. What percentage of people sleep at least 9 hours?
cards.why: 9 = 7.8 + 2 × 0.6, two standard deviations above. 95% are within 2, so 5% are outside, half at each end: 5% ÷ 2 = 2.5%.
cards.hook: Outside the middle 95%: 5%, split equally between the two ends.

cards.q: Scores are normal with mean 100 and standard deviation 20. The top 2.5% get "Exceptional". What is the lowest score that gets it?
cards.why: 95% of scores are between 100 − 40 = 60 and 100 + 40 = 140. The other 5% splits in two, so the top 2.5% starts at 140.
cards.hook: Top 2.5% starts 2 standard deviations above the mean.

cards.q: A poll asks a random sample of 1000 people. What is the 95% margin of error, as a percentage correct to 1 decimal place?
cards.why: 1/√1000 = 0.0316…, which is 3.16…%. The next digit is 6, so round up: 3.2%.
cards.hook: Round at the very end: look at the next digit.

cards.q: In a random sample of 500 Cork students, 12.2% got Excellent; the margin of error is 4.5%. Nationally, 10% get Excellent. Is there evidence Cork is different?
cards.why: Interval: 12.2 − 4.5 = 7.7% to 12.2 + 4.5 = 16.7%. 10% is inside it, so there is no evidence that Cork is different.
cards.hook: Claim inside the interval: no evidence of a difference.

cards.q: Minutes reading per day: 90–120 min: 59 students, 120–150 min: 18, 150–180 min: 10. At most how many students read for more than 100 minutes?
cards.why: For the most, assume all 59 in the 90–120 class read over 100 minutes. Add everyone above: 59 + 18 + 10 = 87.
cards.hook: "At most": assume the whole split class falls on your side.
